examples.problem: Calculate the integral $\displaystyle{\int} (2\sec^2 x + \sec x \tan x )\, \textrm{d}x.$
examples.worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
\int \sec^2 x \, \textrm dx = \tan x + C
$$

and

$$
\int \sec x \tan x \, \textrm dx = \sec x + C.
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
\eqalign{
		\int (2\sec^2 x + \sec x \tan x )\, \textrm{d}x& = 2 \int \sec^2 x \, \textrm{d}x+ \int \sec x \tan x \, \textrm{d}x \
										&=2\tan x + \sec x + C.

}
$$

$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4sin⁡x-3csc⁡x\,cot⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =4\int sin⁡x\,\text{d}x-3\int csc⁡x\,cot⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =4(-cos⁡x)-3(-csc⁡x)+C \\  & =-4cos⁡x+3csc⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
